> 困。亨。貞，大人吉，無咎。有言不信。

Hexagram 47 is about being enclosed, and it is the one genuine picture-character in this series — the proof by which the other ten can be judged.

## 困 is 從木在囗中

說文: 困，故廬也。從木在囗中 — a tree shut inside a frame.

A living thing that cannot grow out.

Which is the counter-example the book needs: ten chapters have corrected phonetic characters read as pictures (訟 從言公聲, 謙 從言兼聲, 觀 從見雚聲, 賁 從貝卉聲, 復 從彳复聲, 妄 從女亡聲, 坎 從土欠聲, 萃 從艸卒聲 …). Their common fault is that a sound was taken for a meaning.

困 is the other kind: both parts carry a meaning, 囗 is the enclosure and 木 is the living thing enclosed.

So being 會意 requires each part to carry its own sense. It is not "there is a shape in the character that looks like something."

## 株木

株: the stump, the part between the root and the trunk; another reading is "a tree without branches or leaves."

初六 臀困于株木 — sitting on a bare stump.

And a correction: later commentators read 株木 as a kind of cangue or shackle. But 株's original sense is a stump, not a yoke.

The 易 takes the image of no shade, not of being clamped: sitting on a dead piece of wood, with nothing overhead, nothing behind, nowhere to hide.

## 幽谷 / 三歲不覿

谷: the watercourse between two hills. 幽: dark.

Into the dark valley — the lowest, darkest, least visible place.

覿: to see. 三歲不覿 — three years without seeing people, or being seen.

## 朱紱 / 赤紱

紱 is the knee-cover worn in front, part of the insignia of office, its colour graded.

困 uses it twice: 九二 朱紱 (vermilion) and 九五 赤紱 (crimson).

One object, two positions, two kinds of being stuck: one has 方來 — the insignia is about to arrive; the other has 困于 — it is trapped by it.

Same garment: on the one who is about to receive it, it is a prospect; on the one who has it, it is a fetter.

## 蒺藜 / 葛藟

蒺藜: a thorned creeper — touch it and you are pricked.
葛藟: kudzu and vine — things that wind around you.

One under the foot, one around the body.

And note what the 易 uses to write 困: dead wood, thorns, vines. It does not say "there are enemies." It says "there are things growing on you."

## 劓刖

六五/九五: 劓 is the cutting of the nose, 刖 the cutting of the foot.

Usually read as an image of constraint above and below: the nose is up and covered by the top line; the foot is down and pulled by the yin lines. Not a literal punishment — the position of being unable to move in either direction, written with the two heaviest characters available.

## 說 means 脫

九五 乃徐有說 — the 說 here is 脫, to come free. Not "to speak."

Read as "speaking," the whole line collapses. Slowly, then free: that is the fifth line.

## 致命遂志

The 象: 君子以致命遂志 — hazard the mandate, accomplish the aim.

致 is to deliver, to hand over. 命 is the charge one has been given.

So: hand over the charge — spend it, do not conserve it — and the aim is achieved.

Which is the only instruction in the chapter that names what to do with a closure: not endure it, spend it.

## The test

Take a constraint you are inside — a role with no route out, a body of work with no audience. Ask what kind of thing is enclosing you: a frame (囗), or thorns and vines that grew there. Then ask the 象's question: is there a charge here that could be spent rather than preserved?
